curatorBrief.title: Short 'a' Word Adventures
curatorBrief.intent: Introduce young learners to the short /a/ vowel sound (as in 'apple' and 'cat') and guide them in blending individual sounds into three-letter CVC words and matching those words to meaningful pictures.

objectiveBlocks.objectiveText: Say the short /a/ sound and blend individual letter sounds together to hear a word

components.title: Hear and Say Short /a/
components.intent: Model the continuous short /a/ vowel sound aloud with the live tutor, practicing onset and medial isolation before blending with consonants like m, s, and t.

components.title: Blend Sounds Together
components.intent: Provide sound-by-sound word-building practice with phoneme tiles for short 'a' CVC families (-at, -an, -am), guiding students to tap letter sounds and blend them to reveal whole words.

components.title: Speak and Blend Words Aloud
components.intent: Engage students in live tutor-judged CVC decoding where the child sees printed short 'a' words (such as 'cat', 'map', 'fan') and blends the sounds out loud.

objectiveBlocks.objectiveText: Identify written CVC words with short 'a' and match them to pictures

components.title: Words and Pictures: Short 'a' Family
components.intent: Introduce concrete picture-word pairings for core short 'a' CVC words (cat, bat, pan, bag) with clear visual anchors and self-check recognition questions.

components.title: Picture Match Challenge
components.intent: Have students decode a printed short 'a' CVC word and tap the corresponding picture to demonstrate reading comprehension and word recognition.

components.title: Spell the Word to Match the Picture
components.intent: Students hear a short 'a' CVC word paired with an illustrated prompt and build the word into Elkonin boxes using letter tiles to reinforce print-sound-meaning correspondence.

finalAssessment.title: Short 'a' Reading Celebration
finalAssessment.intent: Assess student mastery across both objectives with spoken and picture-matching challenges focusing on blending short 'a' sounds and recognizing written CVC words.

data.title: Word Workout: Reading CVC words with short a

problems.question: What word do the sounds /c/, /a/, and /t/ make?
problems.rationale: When we put the sounds /c/, /a/, and /t/ together smoothly, they say the word 'cat'. The middle sound is the short a sound, as heard in the word 'cat'. Words like 'cot' and 'cut' have different vowel sounds in the middle.
problems.teachingNote: Have students practice continuous blending by stretching each sound out (/c/-/aaa/-/t/) before pushing the sounds together quickly to say the word.
successCriteria: Blend the individual phonemes /c/, /a/, and /t/ to form the spoken word 'cat'.
Recognize the short a vowel sound in a CVC word.
problems.subject: LANGUAGE_ARTS

problems.question: Which word finishes the sentence: I look at the ___?
problems.rationale: The word 'map' has the short a sound /æ/ as in apple and makes sense in the sentence. The word 'mop' uses the short o sound /ɒ/, and 'mup' is not a real word. Reading the sounds /m/ /æ/ /p/ together makes the word 'map'.
problems.teachingNote: Kindergarteners often confuse the short a and short o sounds because both require an open mouth. Remind students that short a makes a smiling mouth sound like in 'apple', while short o makes a round mouth sound like in 'octopus'.
successCriteria: Read and identify the short a CVC word 'map'
Distinguish between the short a and short o vowel sounds in CVC words
problems.subject: LANGUAGE_ARTS

problems.question: Which picture matches the word hat?
problems.rationale: The word hat has three sounds: /h/, short /a/, and /t/. Blending these sounds together makes the word hat, which matches the picture of the hat. The other choices show a hen and a hot dog, which do not have the short a sound.
problems.teachingNote: Have students segment each phoneme (/h/ - /a/ - /t/) on their fingers before blending to reinforce short vowel identification.
successCriteria: Decode the short a CVC word hat
Match a short a CVC word to the correct picture
problems.subject: LANGUAGE_ARTS

problems.question: Which of the following is used for cooking?
problems.rationale: A pan is a metal dish used on a stove to cook yummy food. When we blend the letter sounds /p/, /æ/, and /n/, they make the word pan. A bag holds school supplies and a van is driven on roads, so they are not used for cooking.
problems.teachingNote: Encourage students to tap out each sound (/p/ - /a/ - /n/) with their fingers before blending the whole word together and matching it to its meaning.
successCriteria: Decode CVC short a words with accurate letter-sound correspondence
Match decoded CVC words to their real-world meanings
